claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule re-entered Earth's atmosphere on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean west of San Diego on Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET.
The Artemis II Orion capsule separated from its service module at 7:33 p.m. ET on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II Orion capsule hit the upper atmosphere at 7:53 p.m. ET on April 10, 2026.
The re-entry initiated a six-minute communications blackout before landing.
Drogue parachutes deployed at 8:03 p.m. ET on April 10, 2026 during the Artemis II return.
The crew was safely recovered from the Artemis II Orion capsule by NASA and U.S. Navy teams.
The crew was transported to the USS John P. Murtha.
The Artemis II reentry concludes a nearly 10-day mission around the Moon.
Artemis II is the first human-crewed mission to re-enter from lunar distances in over 50 years.
